No. My previous message was wrong: the Great Wall is not visible to the naked eye from the Moon, and it isn't the only human-made structure claimed to be.

From about 384,000 km, no individual human structure is discernible. Even continents show only as large-scale color and cloud patterns. The wall is long but mostly under 10 m wide and built of materials that match the surrounding terrain.

It's also hard to see from low Earth orbit (~400 km). Astronauts, including Yang Liwei, China's first astronaut, have said they couldn't see it unaided. Photos of it from the ISS exist, but they're taken with zoom lenses and under favorable conditions. City lights at night and large features like airports and greenhouses in Spain are more noticeable from orbit.
